texts.preamble: Sailendrabhai Damodarbhai Shah vs The State Of Gujarat on 8 February, 2024 Author: Abhay S. Oka Bench: Abhay S. Oka 1 In The Supreme Court Of India Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction Criminal Appeal No(S). 1606 Of 2010 Sailendrabhai Damodarbhai Shah & Ors.
texts.facts: The Rules have been framed under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short the said Act).
texts.arguments: Sub-Rule (1) of Rule 47 lays down the general rule that no artificial sweetener should be added to any article or food. Sailendrabhai Damodarbhai Shah vs The State Of Gujarat on 8 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147620038/ 1 Provided that aspartame may be marketed as a table top sweetener in tablet or granular form in moisture proof package and the concentration of aspartame shall not exceed 18 mg per 100 mg of tablet or granule. After the learned senior counsel appearing for the appellants pointed out the aforesaid flaws, the learned counsel for the respondent made her best endeavour to satisfy us that even the basic flaw in the complaint will not be fatal. Her submission is that though there may not be any specific averment in the complaint that the appellants were manufacturing and selling table top sweeteners and though, the Food Inspector may not have said that he collected sample of table top sweetener, in fact, the appellants were fully aware that they were not manufacturing zero calorie sweetener and they were manufacturing table top sweetener. Her submission is that the appellants should not be allowed to take advantage of technicality.
